intro.text: A number sign (#) is used with this entry because of evidence that primary coenzyme Q10 deficiency-2 (COQ10D2) is caused by homozygous or compound heterozygous mutation in the PDSS1 gene (607429) on chromosome 10p12.1.

checks.claim: Primary coenzyme Q10 deficiency-2 (COQ10D2) is caused by homozygous or compound heterozygous mutation in the PDSS1 gene.
checks.evidence_quote: carrying three pathogenic variants in the PDSS1 gene, homozygous in one family and compound heterozygote in the other
checks.explanation: Paper describes PDSS1 deficiency (CoQ10 deficiency) with homozygous and compound heterozygous variants; the COQ10D2 label is standard nomenclature.

checks.claim: The PDSS1 gene is located on chromosome 10p12.1.
checks.evidence_quote: a novel homozygous pathogenic variant in PDSS1
checks.explanation: The paper gives no chromosomal location, but standard locus nomenclature counts as a restatement.

paragraphs.text: Primary coenzyme Q10 deficiency-2 (COQ10D2) is an autosomal recessive disorder caused by a defect in PDSS1, which acts in the first step of CoQ10 synthesis. Nardecchia et al. (2021) described the phenotype as clinically heterogeneous. Some patients had sensorineural deafness followed by optic atrophy, together with mild intellectual disability, muscle weakness, and cardiac valvulopathy. Other patients had a severe infantile multisystem disorder that was fatal in early childhood (Bellusci et al., 2021).

checks.claim: Primary coenzyme Q10 deficiency-2 (COQ10D2) is an autosomal recessive disorder.
checks.evidence_quote: This 16‐year‐old girl was born to consanguineous Egyptian parents
checks.explanation: The paper never says 'autosomal recessive'. Recessive inheritance is only implied by homozygous variants in a consanguineous family with carrier parents.

checks.claim: COQ10D2 is caused by a defect in PDSS1.
checks.evidence_quote: Missense PDSS1 mutations in CoenzymeQ10 synthesis cause optic atrophy and sensorineural deafness.

checks.claim: PDSS1 acts in the first step of CoQ10 synthesis.
checks.evidence_quote: PDSS1 and PDSS2 genes encode two proteins (DPS1 and DLP1) implied in the first step of CoQ10 synthesis

checks.evidence_quote: PDSS1 deficiency is a clinically heterogenous rare disorder

paragraphs.text: Nardecchia et al. (2021) summarized the clinical features of the 2 sibs first reported by Mollet et al. (2007): a male examined at 22 years of age and a female examined at 14 years of age. Both sibs had neurosensorial deafness, optic atrophy, mild intellectual disability, and muscular weakness. Both also had cardiac involvement consisting of mild to moderate valvulopathy. Nardecchia et al. (2021) noted that in these sibs the neurosensorial loss came before the optic atrophy. In the summary table, both sibs were listed with lactic acidosis, macrocephaly, peripheral neuropathy, and obesity/livedo reticularis, and neither had failure to thrive or nephrotic syndrome. Brain MRI had not been performed.

paragraphs.text: Nardecchia et al. (2021) reported 2 sisters born to consanguineous Egyptian parents. The proband, a 16-year-old girl, had normal motor development and walked independently at 15 months, but she had a severe language delay. At age 4 years she was found to have profound bilateral sensorineural hearing loss, which was treated with an externally powered prosthesis. After this she could speak simple sentences, but difficulty with verbal comprehension persisted, and mild intellectual disability was later diagnosed. Her visual acuity was reported as normal at 11 years but was 1/10 bilaterally at 14 years. She also had red-green dyschromatopsia, and pupillary light reflexes were normal with no relative afferent pupillary defect. Fundus examination showed optic atrophy that was most marked in the inferior temporal sector. Visual evoked potentials showed increased latency and reduced amplitude of the P100 waveform, and optical coherence tomography showed bilateral thinning of the retinal nerve fiber layer. She had diffuse mild muscle weakness and a mild postural tremor of the upper limbs, and brain MRI was normal. Echocardiography showed a moderately dysplastic mitral valve with moderate insufficiency and medium-grade tricuspid insufficiency, with an estimated pulmonary artery systolic pressure of 40 mmHg, and a moderately dilated left atrium. Her younger sister had bilateral sensorineural hearing loss. At age 6 years she developed decreased visual acuity, and examination showed optic atrophy with bilateral temporal pallor of the optic nerve head, as well as divergent strabismus. Nardecchia et al. (2021) proposed that PDSS1 deficiency be added to the differential diagnosis of optic atrophy associated with sensorineural deafness. They noted that sensorineural deafness seemed to come before optic atrophy in PDSS1 deficiency, which is the reverse of the pattern in OPA1 and OPA3 defects.

paragraphs.text: Bellusci et al. (2021) reported a boy with primary CoQ10 deficiency who had been born prematurely after an in vitro fertilization pregnancy complicated by twin-twin transfusion. At age 5 months he had failure to thrive, hypotonia, feeding difficulties, bilateral hearing impairment, pulmonary hypertension, livedo reticularis, and distal phalangeal erythema. Laboratory tests showed anemia, lactic acidosis, 3-methylglutaconic and tricarboxylic aciduria, and decreased CoQ10 levels in lymphocytes. Brain MRI showed mild cerebral atrophy at 12 months and cystic change in the white matter at 24 months. He went on to develop a progressive multisystem disorder that included severe developmental delay, pyramidal dysfunction, seizures, tremor, optic atrophy, nystagmus, severe visual and hearing impairment, and chronic heart failure. He died at age 3 years. Chronic distal phalangeal erythema was present from age 5 months onward.

paragraphs.text: The transmission pattern of COQ10D2 is autosomal recessive. Mollet et al. (2007) found a homozygous PDSS1 mutation in a family. Nardecchia et al. (2021) reported a homozygous mutation in 2 affected sisters born to consanguineous parents; both parents carried the mutation, and their unaffected sibs were heterozygous or homozygous wildtype. Bellusci et al. (2021) reported a patient with compound heterozygous mutations.

paragraphs.text: In affected members of a family with CoQ10 deficiency (family 1), Mollet et al. (2007) found a homozygous mutation in the PDSS1 gene that changed a conserved amino acid (D308E). The authors concluded that the mutation caused the OXPHOS deficiency.

paragraphs.text: In 2 sisters born to consanguineous Egyptian parents who had sensorineural deafness and optic atrophy, Nardecchia et al. (2021) found a homozygous c.735G-T transversion in the PDSS1 gene by whole-exome sequencing. The variant was predicted to cause a gln245-to-his (Q245H) substitution at a highly conserved position. It was not reported in the gnomAD database and lay in a 12-Mb region of homozygosity. Both parents were heterozygous carriers. Of the unaffected sibs, a sister was homozygous wildtype and a brother was heterozygous.

paragraphs.text: Nardecchia et al. (2021) noted that, among the CoQ10 deficiencies, visual system involvement had been reported only in defects of the very first steps of CoQ10 synthesis. Optic atrophy had been described in PDSS1 defects, optic atrophy combined with retinitis pigmentosa in PDSS2 defects, and retinitis pigmentosa alone in COQ2 defects. They also contrasted the 2 sibs with the homozygous missense mutation reported by Mollet et al. (2007), who had deafness, optic atrophy, and mild intellectual disability, with the much more severe phenotype of the compound heterozygous patient with a missense and a truncating variant reported by Vasta et al. (2012).

paragraphs.text: In a boy with primary CoQ10 deficiency, Bellusci et al. (2021) reported compound heterozygosity for a c.716T-G transversion in the PDSS1 gene, resulting in a val239-to-gly (V239G) substitution, and a c.1183C-T transition, resulting in an arg395-to-ter (R395X) substitution. His disease began at age 5 months and included hearing impairment, pulmonary hypertension, livedo reticularis, distal phalangeal erythema, lactic acidosis, and 3-methylglutaconic aciduria. He developed a progressive multisystem disorder and died at age 3 years.
